answer: An agent marketplace buying orchard surveys, oasis water reports and onyx inspections can cap rewards per verified customer job. A customer commits a task hash before choosing a worker; payment counts toward reputation only after a randomly assigned auditor checks evidence and delivery. Repeated customer-worker pairs share a declining reward budget. Fake identities then need independently funded jobs and convincing evidence instead of free mutual endorsements. Colluding auditors and rich attackers remain risks, while audits add delay and can reject honest work.
